headline: Executive order addresses the use of project labor agreements on federal construction projects.
what_it_does: This order sets federal policy on project labor agreements for construction projects paid for by the federal government. A project labor agreement is a contract made before work starts between the builders and labor unions. It sets wages, work rules, and ways to settle disputes for the whole project. No summary was provided, so the order's specific rules and limits are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Construction companies that bid on federal projects
who_it_affects.how: They may need to agree to a project labor agreement to work on some federal construction jobs.

who_it_affects.group: Construction workers and building trades unions
who_it_affects.how: Their pay and work rules on certain federal projects may be set by a project labor agreement.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that pay for construction
who_it_affects.how: They are given direction on when to use project labor agreements for their building projects.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed February 6, 2009; the effective date is not stated in the provided material.
